name: Traditionalism
summary: Spanish Traditionalism is a political doctrine, formulated in the early nineteenth century, holding that politics must implement Catholic social teaching and Christ's social kingship under a confessional, hereditary monarchy limited by natural law, fundamental laws and the self-government of social bodies. It rejects popular sovereignty, parliamentary democracy, written constitutions, religious and press freedom and the equality of individuals, in favour of an organic, corporative society, regional fueros and the cultural community of Hispanidad. It developed no distinct economic theory and opposed both liberal capitalism and communism.
scope: The Spanish doctrine described in Wikipedia's article Traditionalism (Spain), as formulated by Balmes, Donoso Cortes, Vazquez de Mella, Pradera, Elias de Tejada and Gambra, and adopted as the theory of Carlism. It overlaps heavily with the existing carlism profile (the movement) but here answers for the doctrine as such. It excludes the Carlos Hugo socialist turn, Francoism and the Integrist claim to monopolise the label, and is not Perennialist Traditionalism (Guenon, Evola).

keyFigures.name: Juan Donoso Cortés

sources.usedFor: Donoso's defence of dictatorship as a necessary evil, disillusion with liberalism, view of socialism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Traditionalism developed no health policy; Rerum novarum-style social Catholicism favours charity and corporate bodies, but a state guarantee is not documented either way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No statutory wage doctrine is recorded; the corporative model has trades set pay, which neither endorses nor rejects a state minimum.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sources note hostility to capitalism and no distinct economic theory; the movement preferred corporate and guild order to free markets, inferred from that.

public-ownership.rationale: Wikipedia reports no economic programme and a dislike of the omnipotent dirigiste state, so nationalised industry is inferred as unwelcome.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources document no fiscal doctrine; adherents ranged from hostility to capitalism to defence of private property.

unions-good.rationale: Traditionalists favoured gremial (guild-style) corporations of employers and workers, not class-based unions; they are separated from Francoist syndicalism and from class war.

property-fundamental.rationale: Views ranged from distrust of capitalism to acceptance of private property per the article; property is held subject to Catholic social teaching, so not an absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No programme on firms in the modern sense is documented; corporative regulation by guilds is favoured but business regulation by the state is not discussed.

cut-welfare.rationale: No welfare doctrine documented; social duty is placed on Church, family and corporate bodies, but adherents are not recorded as demanding cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative ideas appear among Rerum novarum-inspired currents, but collective worker ownership of firms is not a traditionalist demand; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalists favour order yet distrust the omnipotent state, so adherents have no recorded stance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; a Catholic moral order opposed to licence makes legalisation unlikely, inferred from the moral-order emphasis.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; they restrict speech that offends Catholic truth (not group hatred), so this statement does not map cleanly.

strong-leader.rationale: Traditionalists wanted strong but highly limited monarchy bound by natural law and fundamental laws, and objected that Franco's caudillaje was incompatible with their doctrine; some accepted dictatorship only as a last resort.

state-harmful.rationale: They defend a Catholic monarchy and a state as part of the natural order, though a light one; abolition of the state is flatly rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the Carlist tradition of armed volunteers (requetes) is not a policy position on civilian ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order and a confessional state point toward support for the forces of order, but sources record no explicit programme; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Catholic moral law as the basis of public order makes legal prostitution contrary to traditionalist doctrine; inferred from the confessional state.

decide-locally.rationale: The fueros and anti-centralism are core: Carlists opposed homogenization and centralism that erased local identities, and championed self-government of social bodies.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; Donoso stressed sin and authority, while Catholic tradition also values reform of offenders, so adherents are split.

traditional-family.rationale: Mella is described as treating the family as the key element of the social fabric, and the Catholic social order is central to the doctrine.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Catholic moral law as the basis of law and the rejection of modern liberal rights make this firmly opposed, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: The doctrine requires politics to implement Catholic teaching, which forbids abortion; not discussed specifically in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Catholicism as state religion and Christ's social kingship are the heart of the doctrine; the article says politics should implement Catholic social teaching.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; rejection of equality of individuals and of egalitarian programmes suggests disagreement, inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Their organic hierarchical, Catholic view of society rests on natural order, not social construction; inferred from that stance.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Tradition is the source of the nation in Mella's account and Hispanidad is the cultural framework they defend.

gradual-change.rationale: They defend inherited institutions yet some Carlists took up arms and conspired; they sought restoration, not gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Catholic unity as basis of the nation implies caution but there is no stated policy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nation-states are said to be incompatible with traditionalism, but supranational secular bodies fit its anti-liberal outlook no better; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Hostility to capitalism and industrialisation and a rural outlook imply scepticism about free trade, inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Traditionalists rejected nationalism in favour of Hispanidad and Catholic universality, so neither pole fits.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; no recorded position on modern human-rights interventions, which they distrusted as liberal doctrine.

open-borders.rationale: A nation built on Catholic unity and tradition cannot be dissolved into open borders; inferred from the doctrine of organic society.

limit-growth.rationale: No documented position; rural, anti-industrial leanings are offset by no explicit environmental argument.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The doctrine predates the issue and takes no position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Donoso rejected the progressive view of history and held that civilisation reflects theology, not technique; secular progress cannot save humanity.

revolution-justified.rationale: They opposed revolutions but justified armed uprising (Carlist wars) against illegitimate liberal rule, so adherents are split in their treatment of the term.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rule is by tradition, Church and social bodies, neither experts nor the general public; the statement does not map.

central-planning.rationale: Traditionalism opposed the omnipotent, dirigiste state, and the sources record no embrace of planning; a planned economy is contrary to organic corporate society.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; worker or public ownership of firms is a socialist idea that Donoso condemned as a product of eroded Christian morality.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The family and hereditary order are central, so heavy inheritance tax is inferred as unwelcome.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a state-provided universal payment cuts against a society of families and corporations, inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Rural orientation and anti-liberal economics suggest protectionist sympathies, but the sources document no trade policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The omnipotent dirigiste state was rejected as incompatible with traditionalism, so state steering of investment is inferred as disliked.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The rural outlook and corporative, Rerum novarum approach favour a distribution of property among families, but the sources only loosely imply it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Donoso treats socialism as a theological error born of atheism, and a doctrine that abolishes wage labour is wholly alien to the corporative order.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banking and monetary design lie outside the sources on Traditionalism, and no inference from its Catholic corporative principles points either way.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporative representation and gremialismo are core, though traditionalists contrasted their free guilds with state-run Francoist syndicalism, which limits the fit with state-recognised bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Traditionalists objected to the Franco regime's single party and wanted a system without parties and with organic representation.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Confessional hereditary monarchy limited by natural law is a core element of the doctrine.

democracy-best.rationale: Traditionalism is described as incompatible with democracy, rejecting popular sovereignty and parliamentarism.

direct-votes.rationale: They reject democracy and popular sovereignty, favouring organic representation in the Cortes of social bodies.

workers-councils.rationale: Representation through trades and corporations is traditionalist, but class councils as the basis of power belong to communism, which they opposed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Carlists opposed Basque and Catalan political ambitions while defending fueros, so secession is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: The doctrine rests on a natural, hierarchical order of society and strong hereditary monarchy, although it grounds this in tradition rather than ability.

political-violence-never.rationale: Carlists fought three civil wars and Carlist paramilitaries trained in the 1930s; violence in defence of the traditional order was accepted.

war-builds-character.rationale: No documented view; the Carlist martial tradition is real but glorifying war as character-building is not recorded.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church and state are distinct but closely linked, the state upholds Catholic orthodoxy and religious freedom is rejected.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law is to be based on natural law and Catholic doctrine as taught by the Church, which is close to but not identical with scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A traditional monarchy holding justice and defence as sovereign functions has no place for privatised courts; inferred from the doctrine of authority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Traditionalists reacted furiously to Nazi racism and defined the nation by Catholic faith and tradition, not ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Donoso treats history as theology and decline, and traditionalism rejects class war explicitly (shared with Fascists as hostility to class war).

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rejection of equality of individuals and a hierarchical organic society.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The doctrine concerns Spanish tradition and its sources record no stance on indigenous land rights; the Hispanic Catholic framework gives no clear inference.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hispanidad affirms the Spanish imperial legacy; reparations are inferred as rejected.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hispanidad as a cultural community of Catholic Spanish-speaking peoples is the traditionalist answer to nationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Donoso condemns liberal secular individualism and grounds order in sin and redemption; self-interest as a moral good is alien.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The doctrine rejects human rights and equality of individuals, putting duty within hierarchical bodies first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; creation theology could cut both ways.

limit-population.rationale: Catholic teaching opposes population control, which follows from implementing Catholic social teaching.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some traditionalists were hostile to capitalism and industrialisation with a rural outlook, but they did not call it a disaster across the board.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Donoso rejects progress as a secular creed and Traditionalists preferred preserving inherited institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Contradicts the Catholic natural-law basis of politics; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by tradition, Church and social bodies is the opposite of algorithmic rule; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption postdates the doctrine and nothing in its principles of authority or privacy settles the question, so it stays neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Traditionalism seeks the restoration of the traditional Catholic order of Spain against liberal modernity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Donoso treats politics as derived from theology and doctrinal truth, not pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: They reject parliamentary liberalism but not elections wholly (Carlists stood for the Cortes); methods were mixed.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources discuss the ends (Catholic monarchy) and tolerate varied means, from elections to armed rising, so no stance on matching means to ends is documented.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Their ideal is a Catholic organic society with rural leanings, not pre-agricultural life. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Corporate society is built on distinct trades and social bodies; abolition is incompatible.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist principle that traditionalists oppose as an error of atheistic socialism; charity is favoured but not as an economic principle.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist formula, not addressed by traditionalism; inferred rejection.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Donoso and traditionalists rejected socialism and class war, so the Marxist theory of exploitation is not accepted.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Donoso denounces socialism, and traditionalists were committed anti-communists. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation contradicts the rural, family-based and property-owning outlook; communism is opposed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Hostility to capitalism exists, but a Marxist theory of imperialism is not part of the doctrine.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is natural and legitimate; the doctrine has no anarcho-capitalist element.

harm-principle.rationale: Politics implements Catholic moral law, so the state restricts conduct beyond harm to others; Donoso rejects neutrality between truth and error.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights of individuals are rejected; society is composed of organic bodies, not free individuals.

conscription.rationale: A confessional monarchy defending the order is not recorded as opposed to conscription; the Carlist militia tradition suggests acceptance.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Opposes liberal market-based political ideas; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is an organic, moral order, not a firm; inferred from the doctrine.

media-academia-power.rationale: Traditionalists denounced liberal press and universities as vehicles of error, but the claim of real power over elected officials is not documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: They rejected Nazi racism, so racial determinism is not part of the doctrine.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families, local communities and corporate bodies, with organic representation in the Cortes, is central to traditionalism.

total-state.rationale: Traditionalists considered Franco's omnipotent, dirigiste state incompatible with their doctrine; Mella held a light state over autonomous communities.

national-rebirth.rationale: Restoration of Catholic Spain after liberal decadence is a theme, though they speak of restoration rather than radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hispanidad was a cultural, not territorial, concept for traditionalists.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Carlist dynastic loyalty is real but authority rests on divine and natural law and fundamental laws, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which sought a modern corporative regime rooted in rural small society.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Donoso asserts objective truth against error ("error has no rights") rather than power-relative knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Donoso and the doctrine ground politics in divinely revealed and natural moral truth.

single-common-good.rationale: Politics is to implement the single order of Catholic social teaching and natural law, not to balance interest groups.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Migration and diaspora rights are not discussed in the sources, and Hispanidad is a cultural community rather than a citizenship doctrine.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; local fueros favour local languages, but there is no stated revival policy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate bodies of employers and workers co-operate, but democratic votes in firms are not part of the doctrine.

school-vouchers.rationale: Early traditionalists wanted Church control of education, which is compatible with funding schools parents choose; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; political freedom in the liberal sense is rejected.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not documented; the monarch is limited by law and Church rather than ruling by example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Popular and national sovereignty are rejected; nation-states are seen as incompatible with traditionalism.

force-without-un.rationale: The doctrine predates the UN and its sources say nothing about multilateral authorisation of force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Donoso builds politics on theology and faith; liberal rationalism is his chief target.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No source discusses the welfare state; the Catholic duty of charity is universal, but a restriction to citizens is equally compatible with an organic national society.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is never discussed; Catholic social teaching stresses both the duty to work and charity toward the needy, so it stays neutral.

class-collaboration.rationale: Corporative bodies unite employers and workers; class war is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving inherited institutions and tradition is the point of the doctrine. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc of states resisting Western powers is not part of the doctrine, whose international concept is the cultural Hispanidad.

workers-nation.rationale: Class-based organisation is rejected; the Catholic community and Hispanidad rather than national proletarian lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hierarchical family-based Catholic order implies distinct roles; the sources note revulsion at the modern display of women in public.

ban-interest.rationale: Medieval Catholic usury doctrine is part of the background but there is no documented traditionalist position today.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: They reacted furiously to Nazi racism, and Catholic universalism contradicts racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist theory of the state; the doctrine takes the state as natural and traditional order. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy postdates the doctrine and the sources record no position.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Catholic unity is the basis of the nation (Mella) but there is no discussion of immigration.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy is a modern claim absent from the sources; traditionalists blamed liberalism and Freemasonry, not immigration policy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party-based parliamentary representation is rejected in favour of organic representation; they objected to parties.

national-mission.rationale: Hispanidad has a Catholic civilising dimension, but a mission to spread a form of government is not recorded.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A hierarchical family order is defended, not criticised.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Donoso says liberalism's principles lead to corruption spreading through government, a general attack on liberal political class.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Catholic moral teaching condemns eugenic coercion; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not documented; inferred from order-oriented outlook.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The doctrine calls for a Catholic state upholding orthodoxy, moral order and education, beyond minimal functions.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racism was rejected by traditionalists, and Hispanidad is a cross-racial Catholic community.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: They reject equality of individuals and human rights as liberal doctrine, though Catholic teaching affirms equal dignity before God; the statement mixes both.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist internal debate with no relevance to traditionalists.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the Hispanidad tradition defends the Spanish imperial legacy, which cuts against a colonial label, but no direct position exists.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Fueros are local traditional laws specific to each entity and Catholic law is the base; uniform liberal codes are opposed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The state upholds Catholic orthodoxy and rejects religious freedom, so propagation of other faiths is restricted.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Early traditionalists wanted Church control of education and later Mella wanted state education structures but not secular neutrality in Catholic Spain.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine; they oppose communism and the dirigiste state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Popular sovereignty is rejected; authority comes from God and tradition.

population-transfer.rationale: Not documented; inferred from Catholic universalism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A state enforcing Catholic order uses force beyond defence, and Carlists took up arms.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Donoso rejects progressive history and social Darwinist liberalism; they preferred cooperation among corporative bodies.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Traditionalists opposed all parties and rejected liberal constitutional order, so defensive democracy does not map.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not addressed; the doctrine concerns limiting the monarch by law and social bodies, which is only loosely related.

separated-powers.rationale: They reject divided sovereignty but support limited power through social bodies and natural law; split reading.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninist idea, opposed by traditionalists as part of communism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching and Rerum novarum approach lend support, but the sources record no programme.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing policy is never addressed in the sources on Traditionalism.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Class conflict is opposed, but the sources do not discuss strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not documented; Catholic teaching rejects Malthusian views.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Catholic unity is the basis of Spanish nation per Mella, but ethnicity is not.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rule by tradition and hereditary monarchy is opposed to lottery democracy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Donoso defended dictatorship as a necessary evil and some traditionalists accepted it as a last resort, but others rejected it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is not documented, and the doctrine has no distinct economic theory according to the Wikipedia article.

party-controls-media.rationale: Traditionalists objected to the single party and the omnipotent state; media control by a party contradicts organic society. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rejection of single party rule and a monarch as head of forces. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed; the sources stress Catholic unity as the nation's basis but give no immigration policy.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The pay of representatives is not discussed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Divided sovereignty is rejected and Europe-as-secular-union has no basis; Hispanidad is cultural rather than a pooled union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A strong confessional monarchy with real royal power is core.

church-by-bishops.rationale: A hierarchical Catholic church governed by bishops is the premise.

clerical-rule.rationale: The state is distinct from the Church, though subordinate to Church doctrine; Integrists went further.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Marxist stance foreign to traditionalism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Donoso says error has no rights and traditionalists rejected freedom of the press, so moral censorship fits.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential elections are not part of the doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Popular recall is a democratic device opposed to organic representation.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not part of the doctrine; its international concept is Hispanidad rather than military bloc strategy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Contradicts property and family order; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Carlist volunteer militias existed, but an armed citizenry as policy is not documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Traditionalists preferred a rural outlook and opposed fascist emphasis on heavy industry.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources record no judgement of educated people as a class, though Donoso attacked liberal rationalism as an intellectual error.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Catholic civilisation is held to be higher and Donoso says civilisation reflects theology.

death-penalty.rationale: Donoso defended harsh authority and capital punishment is in the Catholic tradition at the time; the sources are indirect.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Early traditionalists wanted Church-controlled education; gender equality teaching is against their doctrine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic education would give priority to faith but no stance on evolution is documented.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Catholic moral law as the basis of public order; censorship of morality is within the doctrine.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is never discussed; a nation based on faith and tradition could be read either way.

minority-language-support.rationale: Carlists criticised Francoist repression of Basque and Catalan culture and defended local identities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious freedom is rejected; no special exemptions for other faiths.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Donoso rejects liberal toleration of error; traditionalism upholds custom.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is not covered by the sources on the doctrine.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A postcolonial economic argument that the Spanish doctrine never addresses.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting constitutions by popular assembly contradicts the rejection of constitutions and popular sovereignty; rule rests on fundamental laws.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid economic development was not a traditionalist aim, and the sources show they preferred a rural outlook to industrialisation, so there is no clear stance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic charity favours aid, but no foreign aid doctrine is documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy postdates the doctrine, and no source discusses defence posture.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Hereditary monarchy is the doctrine; popular election of head of state contradicts popular-sovereignty rejection. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise for peace is not addressed by the sources on Traditionalism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is accepted but under Catholic social teaching and Rerum novarum, which ties it to the common good.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is absent from the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Collective defence pacts are not part of the doctrine's documented positions.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation law is not discussed in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The state is to be subordinate to the Church; Gambra and others condemned encroachment.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The monarch stands above parties as unifying sovereign; parties are rejected.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Carlists opposed Basque and Catalan separatism, though they favoured fueros.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Fueros are traditional local law and self-government within a federative monarchy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority derives from God and the monarch is Catholic, but divine descent is not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No fiscal doctrine is recorded; the article says the doctrine developed no distinct economic theory.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic view of original sin and nature suggests innate nature plays a part.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The monarch is limited by natural law, fundamental laws and the self-government of social groups.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration postdates the doctrine, and nothing in its principles bears on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Traditional monarchy with Cortes of social bodies resembles a mixed order but is not framed that way.

leader-cult.rationale: Traditionalists rejected the Francoist caudillaje and fascist mass mobilisation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody policy is not addressed; the family is central but no source discusses separated parents.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist debate irrelevant to the ideology.

land-redistribution.rationale: Communist programme; private property is accepted and class war rejected.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the doctrine has no documented position on refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Hispanidad is cultural and Catholic rather than ethnic irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The state upholds Catholic orthodoxy and rejects religious freedom; punishment of apostasy is inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Traditionalists disliked immodest display but no legal dress code is documented.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed; Traditionalism treats nation-states as incompatible with it but gives no view on monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Hispanidad and iberismo are listed among related concepts, a cultural-historical community.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Local self-governing social bodies and fueros are part of the doctrine.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: This concerns a persecuted minority's strategy, which the sources on Spanish Traditionalism do not address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Donoso says civilisation is the reflex of theology; Marxist materialism is rejected.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is not documented; corporative guilds in fact organise trades collectively, which makes the inference ambiguous.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the sources, and the doctrine has no distinct economic theory.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Majority rule is rejected; authority is bound by natural law.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Corporate representation by family and trade, not gender quotas; egalitarianism is rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs are not documented; the rural outlook might favour self-sufficiency but the sources do not say so.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements are not discussed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: A socialist idea not addressed by Traditionalism, though its moral outlook is Catholic; no documented position.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco theory is not addressed; Carlist risings relied on mass volunteer militias, not a small vanguard, but the sources do not discuss the matter.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary monarchy and hierarchical society are central.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Tradition and Hispanidad are central to identity; education is meant to transmit them.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Catholic Hispanic empire as civilising mission is part of the Hispanidad tradition, inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching the tradition and faith of the nation is meant, though they favour Hispanidad over españolismo.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not discussed in the sources on Spanish Traditionalism.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary issuance is not addressed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Traditionalists criticised capitalism but did not theorise its crises or collapse, according to the sources, so no stance is documented.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Hispanidad is a cultural-political framework toward former Spanish lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development economics is absent from the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist debate irrelevant to the ideology.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Liberal libertarian idea; a Catholic communal order is not individualist in that way.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: They reject constitutions and human rights as liberal doctrine.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaties are not discussed in the sources on Traditionalism.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hereditary rule is a core principle.

minority-veto.rationale: Liberal consent idea; sovereignty rests on authority, not individual consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The monarch is limited by natural law and fundamental laws; Carlists reserved legitimacy to a ruler within them.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The monarch holds strong power and parliamentarism is rejected, though the Cortes embodies social sovereignty.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not discussed in the sources, and Catholic tradition accepts both views of animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the sources; Catholic tradition accepts human dominion with humane treatment, but no source says so for this doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchical Catholic order with social duties of the privileged; charity is expected, inferred from Rerum novarum approach.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Politics is the implementation of Christ's social kingship; withdrawal is contrary.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim that the doctrine never discusses.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is absent from the sources on the doctrine.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources record no rule on native-born office-holding.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist debate with no bearing on Traditionalism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid policy is not in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not documented; Hispanidad is cultural, not a demand for territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Hispanidad framework is Hispanic and Catholic.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Traditionalists were not antifascist as a founding creed, though they differed from Fascists on many points.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They shared hostility to communism and Fascists but rejected the omnipotent state, so condemn both as statist; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographical dispute outside the doctrine's documented scope.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Respect for inherited tradition implies preserving them.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources record no stance, though a family-centred order might support it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on Traditionalism.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal institutions are rejected as foreign to Catholic Spain; each tradition has its own fueros.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Traditionalists differed on dictatorship, and viewed the army as protector of tradition at times (1936) but disputed Franco's rule.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; family is the key social element, but paid domestic labour is a modern idea.

filial-duty.rationale: Family as key element of the social fabric and Catholic fourth commandment imply strong filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign investment policy is not documented, and the doctrine has no distinct economic theory.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic matrimonial law is basis of the state; divorce is rejected. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is a democratic device; organic representation is not delegated.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed; corporative bodies might provide insurance, but the sources do not say.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; property in family hands is preferred over state ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Cortes embodies social sovereignty and limits the monarch, so consent by it is plausible; not documented for budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: Carlists defended local identities and criticised repression of Basque and Catalan culture.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not addressed in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian remedies are alien.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Hostility to capitalism and modernity suggests rejection of consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is not discussed; Carlist legitimist solidarity with foreign Catholic causes is not documented in the sources used.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on Traditionalism.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalist currents exist alongside defenders of property.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The family-centred Catholic order favours large families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not discussed, though fueros make local law a principle.

job-guarantee.rationale: State direction of the economy is disliked.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Authority comes from God and natural order, so obedience to legitimate authority is a moral duty.

non-intervention.rationale: International law of intervention is not addressed in the sources.

industrial-unions.rationale: Guild-style corporations are preferred to unions of either kind.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Traditionalists attacked freemasonry and liberalism as conspiracies, but ethnic or religious minority conspiracy is not the doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Catholic marriage law is central. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not discussed in the sources; the doctrine rejects liberal press freedom but this statement is about government records.

local-production.rationale: Rural orientation and local autonomy suggest support.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchist method; traditionalists favour organised hierarchical bodies.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine rejects both national sovereignty and secular international order, so no stance is documented.

religious-nation.rationale: Catholic unity is the basic building block of the Spanish nation per Mella.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A tributary-system idea not addressed by the sources on Traditionalism.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional self-government (fueros) suggests this, but fiscal policy is not documented.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed, though private property is accepted.

defeat-communism.rationale: Traditionalists shared hostility to communism and class war, and many fought the Republic.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Donoso says politics reflects theology and that Catholicism is humanity's salvation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Hostility to capitalism and industrialisation, and rejection of progress as a creed.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rejects equality of the sexes as modern doctrine.

socialized-care.rationale: Family is the key social element; socialised childcare contradicts it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not documented in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed, though fueros are traditional compacts, so the doctrine may sympathise but says nothing directly.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Self-governing social bodies are favoured but not as cooperative utopias.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not documented; local identities should be respected.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Corporative, Rerum novarum approach is a third path between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not documented; Catholic historical tradition matters, but land claims between peoples are not discussed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a doctrinal matter, but traditionalists are not recorded as deniers; they condemned Nazi racism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Catholic moral law is basis of public order; sources do not document the specific penalty.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Some theorists accepted dictatorship as last resort, but traditionalists objected to the omnipotent state and single party.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The state upholds Catholic orthodoxy and rejects religious freedom and press freedom.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Hispanidad stressed a community of peoples rather than exploitation; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic legal concept outside the doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Carlists fought liberal governments as illegitimate, and legitimacy requires Catholic rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Democracy and popular sovereignty are rejected.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Contrary to Catholic natural-law basis of politics.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic moral law as basis of law.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not documented, though traditionalists claimed to stand outside liberal dichotomies.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept; Donoso rejects socialism but traditionalists also criticised capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Catholic unity is the Spanish identity, but modern Islam debate is absent from the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Politics rests on divine order and Revelation, and Christ's social kingship; Donoso says the Church's authority is holy precisely as divine.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secular neutrality is rejected; Catholic confessional state.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment and legal practice questions are absent from the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: No distinct economic theory; a third way exists but is corporative.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Carlism is a martial tradition defending the order. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is not discussed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc policy is not part of the documented doctrine.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession is core to the monarchist doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is not discussed, though medieval Catholic suspicion of usury sits in the background.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lending policy is absent from the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Suffrage by social bodies rather than property or head count is favoured.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claim opposed to Catholic hierarchical view.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Traditionalists rejected press freedom but on moral grounds, not the Marxist one.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Monarchy limited by fundamental laws and natural law agrees with rule through standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Traditionalists reacted furiously to Nazi racism.

online-participation.rationale: A democratic device contrary to organic representation.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not discussed in the sources, and the question postdates the doctrine.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Catholic marriage law and Catholic unity imply restrictions; sources do not document specifics.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Consumer boycotts of religious minorities are not documented in the sources on this doctrine.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Rule by tradition and corporate bodies, not random citizens.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Gambra opposed Vatican II religious freedom; the doctrine upholds orthodoxy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; corporate order is not libertarian.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Catholic moral law as basis of order.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Donoso says error has no rights and civilisation is the reflex of theology.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Order and authority are central. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power sharing is not addressed; the doctrine's own corporative sharing among social bodies is a different matter.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Social duty is placed on Church, family and corporate bodies per the Catholic social teaching they follow.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources give no position on reunifying nations split by outside borders; Hispanidad is cultural and iberismo is only listed as a related concept.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from Spanish Traditionalism's preference for hereditary monarchy and organic representation over career electoral politics; term limits are not discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of individual suffrage and popular sovereignty in favour of corporate, society-based representation; delegable voting is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine's thinkers; Catholic providentialism could cut either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The doctrine is militantly Catholic and defends the Church's traditional order, in which priesthood and teaching office are male.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Its defence of the traditional Catholic family and hierarchy implies the husband as head of the household, though the sources read do not state this directly.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine rejects the equality of individuals and popular sovereignty, preferring representation through social bodies.

rent-control.rationale: Traditionalism developed no distinct economic theory; Catholic social teaching might support regulation but it is not documented.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: it opposes liberal capitalism but is socially conservative, with no program on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Carlism had youth organisations, but the doctrine itself does not prescribe drilled national youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine does not address nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine does not address foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The doctrine does not address genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social teaching and the doctrine's opposition to liberal capitalism and communism.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Catholic doctrine holds that self-defence and defence of others can justify lethal force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's emphasis on Spain's historical and Catholic continuity and on Hispanidad.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: Catholic natural-law thought treats sex as given by nature; the sources do not discuss it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its organic, natural-law view of society; unaddressed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: a confessional, Catholic doctrine of the Spanish cause that honours its dead as martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The doctrine holds that politics must implement Christ's social kingship, and Donoso Cortes treated political questions as theological.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Hispanidad envisages a cultural community across the Spanish-speaking world rather than a single gathered nation.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: it stresses the organic social and cultural order and fundamental laws as prior to political forms.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: traditional Catholic doctrine uses male language for God; unaddressed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: it treats Church tradition as the standard of judgment, not modern criteria such as women's full humanity.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The doctrine is built on Catholic and regional community, not ethnic economic preference; the sources do not address it.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: its regional fueros follow historic kingdoms and not a merger of regions by people.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's self-governing social bodies and corporative order, which imply autonomous trade bodies; unions as such are not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The doctrine rejects equality of individuals and opposed communism and socialism, so working-class rule is not its test of legitimacy.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No doctrine of public ownership is recorded; corporative bodies or the Church could provide such services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from its organic, corporative representation of social bodies, which suggests a chamber beside any popular one.

municipal-property.rationale: No distinct economic theory is recorded; it opposed both liberal capitalism and communism without naming a property form.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Mella's social sovereignty and regional fueros, which leave self-government with communities and regions.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from its alignment with Catholic social teaching, which defends a family wage; sources do not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Nineteenth-century doctrine with no stated view on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Nineteenth-century doctrine with no stated view on life-extension research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on financial privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's limits on the state by natural law and Catholic teaching, which treats persons as having ends of their own.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The doctrine holds that politics must implement Catholic social teaching and Christ's social kingship, which presumes a spiritual as well as material nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regional fueros are treated as historic rights beyond the legislature's power and the doctrine rejects parliamentary sovereignty.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on genetically engineered crops.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on urban density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's Catholic universalism and its cultural, not racial, community of Hispanidad.

racial-pride.rationale: Hispanidad is a cultural and religious community, not a racial one; the sources say nothing on racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Catholic just-war thought allows more than self-defence, but the sources record no view on the question.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Hispanidad is a cultural community, but Traditionalists tied the nation to Catholic unity, monarchy and regional fueros rather than language alone; inferred from those sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Traditionalists wanted representation through organic social bodies (corporations, regions, estates) rather than individual suffrage; separate religious electorates are not documented, so this is inferred from corporative representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The doctrine blamed liberalism and revolution rather than named foreign partition plots; nothing documented either way.

free-public-college.rationale: No documented position; Traditionalists favoured Church-controlled education, and state-funded tuition is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the doctrine's rejection of liberal capitalism and state intervention beyond natural law, with no sign of support for market-style green taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the organic view of society as a bond across generations and the stress on tradition and inheritance; no environmental application is documented.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic family-centred view of complementary roles for women; the claim that these values deserve more weight in public life is not documented.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; a confessional monarchy values national defence, while Catholic social teaching favours peace, so adherents are split by inference.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of liberal parliamentary publicity and the monarch's prerogative in foreign affairs; no explicit statement on secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: The doctrine developed no distinct economic theory and opposed both liberal capitalism and communism, so capital flows are not addressed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A confessional monarchy under natural law keeps order through the crown, though the sources do not discuss private arms and Carlist tradition included militias; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Traditionalism upholds loyalty to king and altar, and Carlist doctrine favoured a legitimate monarchy's wars; refusal of orders is not supported by the sources; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The corporative society of guilds and social bodies implies collective regulation of trades, but no source states a position; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No documented position; social Catholicism favours charity and corporate bodies, but top-ups are not discussed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The sources show no position on fiscal rules; the doctrine is concerned with sovereignty and religion.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Hispanidad suggests a cultural community with Latin America, but no source describes an economic restructuring programme.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The doctrine defends the historic monarchy and its institutions against revolution, so smashing the state conflicts with it; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Traditionalism upholds a fixed Catholic social order and fueros, not an open blueprint; self-governing social bodies make it partly sympathetic, hence only mild disagreement.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources do not address this; nineteenth-century doctrine predates ecosystem accounting.

sacred-nation.rationale: Traditionalism holds the nation as an organic historical community rooted in Catholic tradition and Hispanidad, outlasting its members.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Corporate bodies and charity rather than state relief are favoured, and no source discusses student loans; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The doctrine defends regional fueros but the sources do not describe an exploitation theory.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Donoso Cortes and the Traditionalists rooted dignity and rights in a Catholic natural-law view of human nature that cannot be redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: The doctrine placed press and education under Catholic orthodoxy and social bodies, so state-funded neutral media is unlikely to be welcomed; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Spanish Traditionalism held that the Catholic religion is the single true one and rejected religious freedom, so it would deny that all religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from corporative social Catholicism and its opposition to liberal capitalism, which protected agrarian rural communities; the sources do not discuss price supports.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its Hispanidad nationalism and support for national strength, with no text on nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: it favoured corporative bodies with workers and employers together against class parties and socialism, not independent labour parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic natural-law morality, which would condemn mutilation, though the doctrine never addressed it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: an organic, family-centred hierarchy rejecting equality of individuals would resist equal legal rights over land; family law was not discussed directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the cultural community of Hispanidad and Spain's regional unity; the sources do not discuss Catalan or Valencian naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The doctrine had no economic theory and does not address liability law; adherents could favour corporative regulation or common-law courts.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Its fueros and self-governing social bodies and rejection of individual popular sovereignty favour customary and corporate bodies with a role in lawmaking; inferred for chiefs by analogy.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine rejects liberal individualism but did not address environmental policy.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its defence of authority and natural-law justice, but it left no detail on sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its Catholic and Hispanic cultural community, which expects immigrants to join the national culture; not discussed in the sources.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Corporative society of self-governing social bodies could include guild membership, but the sources do not discuss compulsory union dues.

voter-id.rationale: The doctrine rejects popular sovereignty and parliamentary democracy, but the sources say nothing on identification at the polls.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The sources say Traditionalists rejected religious freedom and required the state to uphold Catholic orthodoxy, so one interpretation holds legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: It rejects popular sovereignty and parliamentary democracy; legitimacy comes from Catholic social order and natural law, not from competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Implied by the doctrine's requirement that politics implement Catholic social teaching and protect the family.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from Donoso Cortes's defence of dictatorship as a necessary evil and the doctrine's stress on authority and order.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from social Catholicism favouring charity and corporate bodies over a state cash-transfer system; the doctrine has no documented welfare policy.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the equality of individuals and its family-based organic representation; not stated for women specifically.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Its Catholic social order treats religion as the foundation of family and society, so blaming religion for women's oppression would be rejected.

race-social-construct.rationale: The sources do not address race; the doctrine centres on Hispanidad as a cultural community, and adherents have no documented position.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of equality of individuals and its defence of the family; dedicated state agencies for gender equality are not documented.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The sources give no theory of first acquisition; inferred from the Catholic view of property as limited by social function and natural law, which does not make first claim decisive.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's stress on national sovereignty under Christian kingship and its distrust of supranational bodies; it never addressed international tribunals.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Catholic orthodoxy: Scripture is without error, but the Church's authority interprets it, so plain literal reading is not the doctrine's own line.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the equality of individuals and defence of organic, customary social bodies; mandated gender equality in self-rule sits badly with that.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The doctrine opposed communism and socialism as well as liberalism, so a planned state is not worth defending even against restoration.

indirect-election.rationale: Representation runs through corporative social bodies and regions rather than individual voters, which fits delegation upward from lower bodies.

national-church-status.rationale: Sources state that the doctrine requires a confessional state upholding Catholic orthodoxy and rejects religious freedom.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Regional fueros and the self-government of social bodies are core, so regions with a distinct community should govern many of their own affairs.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of popular sovereignty; territorial status would rest on history, dynastic right and tradition, not a local vote.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the respect for inherited historical institutions and the Hispanidad community of peoples; the doctrine did not address decolonisation borders directly.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic critique of liberal materialism and capitalism; the sources do not discuss simple living as an ideal.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The doctrine never addressed indigenous homelands; it values organic communities but also Hispanidad and Catholic mission, so the inference is split.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the defence of the traditional family and distinct social roles; a draft limited to men would not trouble an adherent.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Spanish Traditionalism stresses the organic nation, Hispanidad and the patria, so a bond with ancestral land is inferred, but the sources do not state it as a doctrine.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Traditionalism holds the monarchy limited by natural law and fundamental laws, so killing without trial is inferred to be unacceptable; not discussed directly.

close-ties-china.rationale: The doctrine is anachronistic on China and focuses on Hispanidad and Catholic Europe; no position can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The cultural community of Hispanidad suggests concern for Spanish-speaking kin abroad, but this is inferred, not stated in the sources.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The doctrine developed no distinct economic theory, so no position on common ownership of resources can be inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: It rejects the equality of individuals and sees society as organic and corporative, so individual self-ownership is inferred to be disfavoured.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The doctrine developed no distinct economic theory and the sources do not discuss taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Catholic social teaching favours aid to the poor but the sources give no view on targeting versus universality.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Traditionalism defends the self-government of social bodies against the state, so bypassing intermediate groups is inferred to be contrary to it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: It opposed liberal capitalism but developed no distinct economic theory; no position on business privileges is inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The doctrine demands a confessional Catholic state, so keeping politics free of religion is contrary to it, though denominational parties are not discussed directly.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Traditionalists accepted material progress under Catholic order and tradition; inferred from its rejection of liberalism, not stated on technology.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Traditionalism upholds Catholic social teaching and an organic hierarchical family, and rejects the equality of individuals, so a wife's unilateral divorce is contrary to it.

national-resource-control.rationale: The doctrine developed no distinct economic theory and the sources do not address resource control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: No doctrine of distributive justice is documented; corporative order and charity are favoured, which pulls both ways.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: No fiscal doctrine on financial transactions is recorded; inferred as outside the doctrine.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Spanish Traditionalism did not address this question; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The doctrine holds monarchy is limited by natural law and fundamental laws, consistent with the natural-law view that a law contrary to it does not bind.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic for the nineteenth-century doctrine; no source addresses automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Hispanidad and regional fueros are favoured but a world order is not addressed; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Donoso Cortes opposed socialism, so the Marxist labour theory would likely be rejected; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The corporative, organic society values workers' bodies and love of the Catholic Spanish homeland; inferred from the organic model.

material-over-identity.rationale: Traditionalism opposes the left generally and does not address left strategy; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Traditionalism opposed both liberal capitalism and communism, and communist party rule is incompatible with a Catholic monarchy.

missingStatements.text: Political sovereignty belongs to society's natural communities, such as families, regions and trades, rather than to the state or the individual voter.
missingStatements.rationale: Mella's social sovereignty makes communities self-governing and the state a light superstructure; this is the doctrine's signature political theory.

missingStatements.text: The state should not treat different religions as equals; the true religion may be given legal privilege over others.
missingStatements.rationale: The sources say Traditionalists rejected religious freedom and required the state to uphold Catholic orthodoxy.

notes: Many answers on economics and modern issues are inferred because the sources say no distinct economic theory was developed. Integrists would go further on Church rule over the state; Francoist-leaning Carlists accepted more dictatorship.
